rows.author: C095
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE POSITION OF PROVINCIAL, CITY AND MUNICIPAL ADMINSTRATOR AS A PRIMARILY CONFIDENTIAL POSITION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 480 (a), ARTICLE TEN, TITLE FIVE, BOOK III OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The municipal, city and provincial adminsitrators must work closely with their chief executives in plotting strategies, plans and programs for the development of their respective units.  The administrator's performance is reflective of the mayor's/governo r's accomplishments .  As such, the administrator must enjoy the fullest trust and confidence of his superior to ensure an effective and smooth flow of vital infrastructure, cultural and socio-economic programs and projects.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2000-02-22

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF R.A. 8550, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `THE PHILIPPINE FISHERIES CODE OF 1998'(PREFERENT IAL RIGHTS OF MUNICIPAL FISHERFOLK)
rows.abstract: This bill, therefore, seeks to amend certain provisions of the Fisheries Code in order to strengthen the preferential rights of municipal fisherfolk over the use of municipal waters, put more substance in fisherfolk participation by giving them better representation in the national and local FARMCs, ban destructive fishing gears and methods, as well as facilitate the immediate establishments of fisherfolk settlement areas in coastal communities.

The total annual premiums based on the acturial study of the GSIS shall be included in the General Appropriations Act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE PUBLICATION IN THREE (3) NEWSPAPERS OF NATIONAL AND GENERAL CIRCULATION THE LIST OF RECOMMENDEES FOR EXECUTIVE CLEMENCY, PENALIZING THE FAILURE THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The publication of the names of the recommendeed for executive clemency shall be made at least thirty (30) days prior to the submittal by the Chairman of the Board of Pardons and Parole to the President of the Philippines of the list of recommendeesfor executive clemency.  Any violation of this Act by the Chairman and the Members of the Board of Pardons and Parole shall be punishable by a fine of P10,000.00 or imprisonment of six (6) months, or both at the discretion of the court.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2000-02-22

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE MANDATORY LABELLING OF FOOD AND FOOD PRODUCTS CONTAINING GENETICALLY-MOD IFIED ORGANISMS AND THOSE PRODUCED BY GENETIC ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7394, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CONSUMER ACTOF THE PHILIPPINES, AND REPBULIC ACT NO. 3720, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FOOD, DRUG AND COSMETIC ACT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Concerns about the effects of genetically-mod ifies organisms (GMOs) or those produced through genetic engineering on the environment and the health of the people have been raised lately. With these diverse concerns, it is important consumers be made aware of the issues relevant to the use GMOs, and be given the choice, especially for food products. This measure, therefore, requires the mandatory labelling of food and food products containing GMOS and those produced by genetic engineering technologies. This will, in the process, amend certain existing laws, including the Consumer Act of the Philippines and the Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2000-02-23

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE ALLOWANCE OF PERSONAL EXEMPTION FOR INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS AND THEIR DEPENDENTS AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE OF SECTION 35 (A) AND (B) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: This bill provides for a basic personal exemption as follows:(1) For single individual  or married individual judicially decreed as legally separated with no qualified dependents P30,000.OO;(2) For head of family P35,000.00; and (3) For each marriedindividual P42,000.00. Provides , likewise, for an ADDITIONAL exemption for DEPENDENTS in the amount of TWELVE THOUSAND PESOS (P12,000.00) for each dependent not exceeding four (4).
rows.status: Substituted by HB12423

rows.author: B016
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ADDITIONAL RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO MEMBERS OF THE JUDICIARY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 910, AS AMENDED AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is of common knowledge that the remuneration accorded to the Justices of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeals and other members of the Judiciary  is indecently low.  In response to the call of duty in the administration of justice, most of them have  had to forego lucrative opportunities elsewhere, yet after having made a noble sacrifice ahd having devoted the best years of their lives to public service, they are not afforded appreciable security after retirement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2000-02-23

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL EXEMPTION OF TWENTY THOUSAND (P20,000.00) PESOS FOR MARRIED INDIVIDUALS WHOSE SPOUSE IS A NON-WORKING SPOUSE AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SEC. 35 (A), OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: Rationale: Many non-working spouses are college graduates and some have college units but opted not to work and decided to stay home to take care of the children. These people value their family very much instead of working to earn more money. Justas the State recognizes the Filipino family as the foundation of the nation, it is but fitting to provide these citizens (the non-working spouses who take care of the family) a tax relief by granting them additional individual exemption of P20,000.00.
rows.status: Substituted by HB12423
